newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Walibi says heading for 1996 loss.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Walibi says heading for 1996 loss.

text.p: Belgian holiday parks operator Walibi NV said it was heading for a loss on current operations in 1996 after attendance at its sites this summer fell.
"Weak activity will result in a significant loss in the current result for the present exercise," Walibi said in a statement on first half 1996 earnings.

Its parks in Belgium, France and the Netherlands had attracted 2.95 million visitors by August 31, down from 3.26 million in the same 1995 period. Sales were down eight percent at 2.35 billion Belgian francs from 2.55 billion.
The company forecast that operating cash flow for the whole year would be around 560 million Belgian francs, down from 758 million in 1995.
"The board considers 1996 as a setback which hides some achievements, but does not fundamentally threaten the group's plan of development...," the company said.
The company said it would clamp down on investment expenditure and operating costs.
"This control will enable us, among other things, to realise from 1997 supplementary economies in terms of operating costs of 170 million Belgian francs," it said.
The company said it was confident to be able to "rapidly realise results that conform with the hopes of shareholders."
Walibi's loss in the year to June 30 widened to 418.5 million francs from 395.6 million in the 1995 period on sales of 888.1 million francs, up from 840.8 million.
The company noted it traditionally books only one third of its sales in the first six months of the year. Walibi had a 1995 net profit of 14 million Belgian francs -- its first profit since 1992.
